Jamal K.: Quick Q — planning to start parental leave 2026-05-01. Can I stack accrued vacation so I can be off through 2026-06-01?
Michelle (People Ops): Yes — you may apply PTO on top of company-paid parental leave. There are payroll and benefits steps. Looping in Sara. :wave:
Sara (Benefits): You can stack PTO. Two decisions: (1) apply PTO as leave (counts as continuous service) or cash out, and (2) any temporary FTE change on return? Both affect premiums/HSA.
Jamal K.: I prefer PTO applied (not payout) so service stays continuous. Also thinking of 4 weeks at 80% FTE after I return to ease back in — will that change health coverage?
Lena - Eng Mgr: From team side, 80% for a month is fine. Ill update on-call and coordinate coverage. Ping Eng staffing when you submit. :+1:
Sara (Benefits): Short-term 80% usually keeps active coverage; premiums may be prorated on payroll. Employer HSA contributions could be prorated for partial-pay periods. We need the exact dates to calculate cost share.
Jamal K.: Is there a special form to apply PTO to parental leave, or just the Parental Leave request with a note?
Michelle (People Ops): Submit the Parental Leave request in the HR portal and add comment "PTO applied"; attach a screenshot of PTO balance if helpful. We'll mark the record so Payroll codes it as parental + PTO. Temporary FTE ramps require a signed FTE amendment (we have a template).
Payroll Bot: Reminder: submit leave+PTO combos before the payroll cutoff to ensure correct gross/pay coding. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/leave-forms
Jamal K.: One more — does equity vesting continue during PTO-topup weeks versus unpaid leave?
Emma (Comp & Equity): PTO-applied weeks count as continuous service; vesting continues. Unpaid leave beyond company-paid parental time pauses vesting. Temporary FTE reductions do not pause vesting. Ill update the vesting calendar after you confirm dates.
Jamal K.: Thanks. Ill submit today: 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-01 (first 6 weeks company-paid, last 2 weeks PTO-applied). Ill attach the FTE amendment for a 80% ramp starting 2026-06-02 for four weeks.
Michelle (People Ops): Great — include "PTO applied" in comments and attach the FTE amendment. Ill route to Payroll & Benefits and queue manager signature. Congrats in advance! :tada:
Lena - Eng Mgr: Ill approve the FTE amendment when its in and handle handoffs/on-call.
Jamal K.: Appreciate it everyone — DMing Michelle the docs now. :pray:
